questions.question: What does the machine do (e.g. pump liquids, compress gas, generate mechanical power, cut or shape material, refrigerate)?
questions.why: Headings within chapter 84 split by the machine's function (pumps, compressors, engines, refrigerating equipment, machine tools, and so on).

questions.question: What is the machine used for, or in which application (e.g. agricultural, industrial, domestic)?
questions.why: National lines within many chapter 84 subheadings split further by end use or application.

title.en: Automatic data processing machines; portable, weighing not more than 10kg, consisting of at least a central processing unit, a keyboard and a display

candidates.rationale: Heading 8471 is where the precedents class USB-C docks and hubs used with laptops, and this is the only general ADP-machine subheading offered. The fit is imperfect because the dock is not itself a portable computer with CPU, keyboard and display.

evidence.excerpt:
(A)

For the purposes of heading 8471 , the expression 'automatic data-processing machines' means machines, capable of

(1)

storing the processing program or programs and at least the data immediately necessary for the execution of the program;

(2)

being freely programmed in accordance with the requirements of the user;

(3)

performing arithmetical computations specified by the user; and

(4)

executing, without human intervention, a processing program which requires them to modify their execution, by logical decision during the processing run.

candidates.rationale: A dock is a connectivity device that could loosely be considered network or communication apparatus in heading 8517. Base stations are wireless network infrastructure, so this is a poor fit.
candidates.set_aside_reason: It covers wireless base stations, not a wired peripheral hub for a notebook.
